prompt: In many countries people are having their first child at a much later age than previous generations did. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this development.
essay:
Almost everything good about having children later happens immediately, and almost everything difficult about it happens either at the edge of biology or twenty years downstream. That asymmetry, rather than any disagreement about the facts, is what makes the development hard to evaluate.

The immediate case is strong and not really disputable. People in their thirties tend to have somewhere stable to live, an income that does not disappear if one shift is missed, and a clearer sense of what they are agreeing to. For women the calculation is sharper still, because the years in which careers are decided and the years in which fertility is highest are the same years, and an employment system that punishes absence makes waiting the rational response to a problem the individual did not create.

The costs are of two entirely different kinds. One is biological and personal: fertility falls with age, the treatments that compensate are expensive, arduous and frequently unsuccessful, and a proportion of people who intended to have two children will have one or none. This is a real loss, and it is invisible in aggregate figures because it is recorded as a choice. The other is collective and delayed. A society in which everyone postpones does not merely have its children later; it has fewer of them, and it discovers this a generation after the decisions were taken, when the working population supporting a large retired one turns out to be small.

Discussing the two sides is therefore slightly misleading, because they are not competing accounts of the same thing. The advantages are enjoyed by identifiable people now, and the disadvantages are borne partly by those same people later and partly by people not yet born. If I had to place the weight anywhere, I would put it on the observation that most of the delay is a response to insecure housing, insecure work and unaffordable childcare — which suggests the development is less a preference to be assessed than a symptom to be read.
title: Starting a family later
